author_statement: Author reports splitting commercial academic EPUB chapters with valid footnote anchors. Self-file-qualified hrefs can retain the wrong chapter after split; fragment-only links behave differently. Early author comments say all anchors exist and no warning appears. The author says newest version, without numeric build.
version_limit: 0.9.17 was released before report on same day; operational pin only. Initial body revision and exact installed version unknown.
research_question: Preserve the actual internal-link target after splitting/moving a chapter, including fragment names reused by other chapters. The two-chapter duplicate-id case is researcher-authored, not reported by #450.

conditions.text: An existing link must still reach the same footnote content when splitting separates the reference and target.
Other chapters using the same fragment name retain their own target; fragment names are not assumed unique across chapters.

interface: Book::CreateSectionBreakOriginalResource/CreateNewSections updates split-derived files with AnchorUpdates::UpdateAllAnchorsWithIDs, then other chapters through UpdateExternalAnchors with originating filename. GetIDLocations returns QHash<QString,QString> keyed by id over supplied files. Update methods parse hrefs and SetText when changed. SetText updates GUI document or worker cache; SaveToDisk is separate. Single-section path saves a new working resource before anchor reconciliation. No atomic final EPUB transaction or runtime test provided.

cases.condition: One id in one original chapter; valid unique target.

actions: move its second segment to Text/parts/ch1_tail.xhtml
observe: relative paths from each reference base
cases.condition: Same fragment spelling in distinct source documents; path scope is significant.

actions: attempt to preserve original reference target
